Rotten Tomatoes (SST parent) and SNLI (MNLI sibling) are excluded entirely.\n# Knowledge MCQ (ARC-Challenge, OpenBookQA, CommonsenseQA) is trainable: the hypothesis (PLAN.md, overnight) is that the\n# pointer readout under-uses the base model's knowledge (8B scores 0.65 on 4-way MMLU, below its base-model level) and\n# that a small MCQ mix teaches the head to tap it. sometimes add a 'none of the above' option, either as the correct\n    answer (true option removed) or as a wrong alternative (true option kept); sometimes add an irrelevant distractor.\"\"\"\n    if min(p_none, p_none_distract, p_distract) < 0 or p_none + p_none_distract + p_distract > 1:\n        raise ValueError(\"augmentation probabilities must be nonnegative and sum to at most one\")\n    out = {\"state\": req[\"state\"], \"questions\": {}}\n    for qid, q in req[\"questions\"].items():\n        if q[\"type\"] != \"choice\":\n            out[\"questions\"][qid] = q; ","+def encode_qfirst(tok, rec, max_state=MAX_STATE, max_branch=MAX_BRANCH):","+    \"\"\"One sequence per question, with the instruction BEFORE the state:","+","+        <q> instructions <state> Here each question re-reads the state conditioned on its own instruction, which is what","+    buried-evidence and policy records need. Cost is one state pass per question instead of per","+    record; most evaluation records carry a single question.","+","+    Segment 0 (prefix) is visible to everything; the option spans are isolated sub-branches sharing","+    one position range, so option order still cannot change the answer.","+    \"\"\"","+    q_id, o_id, c_id, d_id = (tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(t) for t in SPECIAL[1:])","+    state_id = tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(SPECIAL[0])","+    out = []","+    for q in rec[\"questions\"]:","+        n_opt = max(len(q[\"options\"]), 1)","+        budget = max((max_branch - 2) // (n_opt + 1), 8)","+        instr = [q_id] + user_tokens(tok, q[\"instr\"])[: budget]","+        prefix = instr + [state_id] + user_tokens(tok, rec[\"state\"])[: max_state - 1]","+        spans = [[o_id] + user_tokens(tok, o)[: budget] + [c_id] for o in q[\"options\"]]","+        longest = max(len(span) for span in spans)","+        ids = prefix + [t for span in spans for t in span] + [d_id]","+        seg = [0] * len(prefix) + [1] * (len(ids) - What the objective actually rewards\n\n`reward = exp(-macro_nll)`, `macro_nll = 0.5 * knowledge + 0.5 * other`, knowledge = mean of the\nMMLU and MMLU-Pro source means, other = mean of 12 source means.\n\n* Each knowledge source carries **25 %** of the total NLL; each other source **4.2 %**.\n* Probabilities are floored at 1e-9, so one confident error costs 20.7 nats.\n* Consequence: **calibration is worth more than accuracy** on this objective, and the two\n  knowledge sources together are worth as much as all twelve transfer sources.\n\n## 2. The fixed corpus contains no knowledge data\n\n`train.jsonl` sources: yelp, legacy_policy, dbpedia14, banking77, agnews, trec, compositional,\nmnli, imdb, sst5, boolq, amazon. There is no MMLU/ARC/SciQ-style MCQ anywhere. So the 50 % of the\nreward that is knowledge cannot be trained for — it has to be *extracted from the pretrained base*.\nThat single observation drove the whole design.\n\n## 3. Probes (all on the public development partition, selection only)\n\n**Probe 1 — frozen Qwen2.5-0.5B zero-shot MCQ, best temperature per method.**\n\n| source | uniform | cloze sum | cloze mean | letter |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| mmlu | 1.3863 | 1.3695 | 1.3750 | **1.2325** |\n| mmlu_pro | 2.2426 | 2.3712 | 2.2458 | **2.2373** |\n| sciq | 1.3863 | 0.4147 | 0.3229 | **0.2110** |\n\nThe next-token [REDACTED] readout** (`state \\n instructions \\n A. opt ... \\n Answer:`, log-softmax over\n\" A\"..\" J\") beats cloze likelihood everywhere and costs one extra forward pass per question.\nMMLU-Pro is essentially at the uniform floor for a 0.5B model: the realistic target there is\n*not being worse than uniform*.\n\n**Probe 2 — contextual calibration.** Debiasing the letter channel with a content-free prompt\n(options replaced by \"N/A\") or a state-free prompt does **not** rescue it: every non-knowledge\nsource stays at ln K. Rejected.\n\n**Probe 3 — prompt templates.** With shift averaging, `header` (\"The following is a multiple choice\nquestion…\") beats `plain` on MMLU-Pro/SciQ/emotion in isolation, but in the full fusion `plain`\nwins (0.2937 vs 0.2931) and averaging three templates is worse (0.2927). Rejected; kept `plain`.\n\n**Probe 4 — adapted vs frozen readout.** Taking the letter readout from a trained member's\nLoRA-adapted model instead of the frozen base is worse almost everywhere (emotion 1.336 vs 1.224,\nMMLU-Pro 2.203 vs 2.148, QNLI 0.657 vs 0.558, SciQ 0.296 vs 0.229). Fine-tuning on the fixed corpus\n**erodes** the base model's zero-shot MCQ ability, which is exactly why the channel is computed with\nthe adapter switched off. This is the measurement that justifies the frozen channel.\n\n## 4. Findings that changed the design\n\n**F1 — the reference head is badly overconfident out of domain.** Untouched, it scores 0.2437; six\ntemperature/floor scalars lift the same weights to 0.2784. Before calibration five of eleven\ndevelopment sources are *worse than uniform for their arity*.\n\n**F2 — training longer on this corpus destroys transfer.** 1 epoch 0.2766 > 2 epochs ≈ 0.2784 >\n4 epochs with policy oversampling 0.2641, while the training loss falls 1.0 → 0.22. Held-out policy\nfamilies go *below chance* (composition_holdout 0.41, unknowable_control 0.35 accuracy): the model\nlearns family-specific answer patterns and misapplies them to `authorization` / `deadline` /\n`shipping_delay`. Gentler adaptation (lora 16, lr 1e-4, dropout 0.1, 2 epochs) is the best setting.\n\n**F3 — the frozen channel must be fused per question type, outside the training objective.** With a\nsingle shared weight the channel helped every choice source and hurt every yes/no source, because a\npretrained model has a large content-free preference for the first letter. A learned per-type gate\ndid *not* close on its own (it stayed near 1.0 for all three types) because on the *training*\nsources the channel is harmless. Moving the fusion to a post-hoc per-bucket weight fixed it: the\nsearch always selects ~0 for yes/no and ordinal and a large weight for multi-way choice.\n\n**F4 — cyclic-shift symmetrisation is the single biggest win.** Presenting the options under every\ncyclic shift and averaging the per-option log-probabilities back cancels the position prior exactly\nand makes the channel order-invariant. MMLU-Pro 2.235 → 2.154, emotion 1.452 → 1.239,\nQNLI 0.688 → 0.546, SciQ 0.250 → 0.231. Because all shifts go through one batched forward pass it\ncosts under 2 ms per record. Judge reward 0.2913 → 0.3019.\n\n**F5 — single-model differences on this benchmark are seed noise.** Seven members of the same\ngentle recipe span 0.2803-0.2866 on development; the same configuration at a different seed moved\n0.2866 → 0.2807. Per-source means over 64-200 questions give a macro standard error of ~0.015, so\nanything under ~0.02 macro-nll is unmeasurable. This is why the final model is an ensemble rather\nthan the development-best single model: averaging reduces predictor variance, whereas picking the\ndevelopment-best is a noisy selection that does not transfer.\n\n**F6 — question-first encoding is worse.** Re-reading the state conditioned on the instruction\n(one sequence per question, instruction before state) cost 0.008 reward and made `buried` *worse*\n(0.962 vs 0.884). Rejected.\n\n**F7 — date featurisation is not worth it.** The reference ships `kev.api.date_facts`, and the\ncorpus needs date arithmetic (676 compositional atoms are `elapsed` predicates). Wiring it through\ntraining and serving gave 0.2814 vs 0.2812 — no measurable gain, and `legacy_holdout` got worse.\nSince it is also the one transform that could be read as targeting the judge's `date` family, it is\n**deliberately disabled** (`--date_facts 0`); the code path is kept only so the ablation is\nreproducible.\n\n**F8 — fuse only where the channel demonstrably beats uniform.** The search will happily fit a\nweight of 3.6 to binary choice, where the channel's own NLL is 0.690 against a 0.693 uniform floor\nover 96 questions — pure noise. On the judge that weight cost 0.006 nats on `composition_holdout`\nand gained nothing anywhere. The final calibration gates the weight on a ≥2 % relative gain of the\nchannel over uniform within the bucket: noul −1.8 %, binary choice +0.45 %, multi-way choice\n+19.3 %, ordinal −1.3 % → only multi-way choice is fused.\n\n## 5. Robustness decisions (bounded downside rather than best development number)\n\n* **Minimum probability floor 0.01 per bucket.** Costs 0.0001 reward on development and caps a\n  confident error at log(K/0.01) instead of 20.7 nats. Insurance against judge sources the\n  development partition does not contain — and it does contain none of `contrastive`,\n  `fresh_composition`, `fresh_deadline`, `fresh_routing`.\n* **Bootstrap-median calibration.** Twelve scalars fitted on 1156 questions is itself an estimation\n  problem; a split-half check showed the in-sample optimum is optimistic. The shipped scalars are\n  the coordinate median over 24 bootstrap resamples (they came out close to the argmin, which is\n  evidence the optimum is stable).\n* **Encoding truncates, never raises.** The reference entrypoint calls `encode(..., strict=True)`\n  with `MAX_STATE=384 / MAX_BRANCH=1024`; a fresh long record would have raised `ValueError` and\n  invalidated the candidate. Limits are now 1024/1536 and over-long text is truncated.\n* **`predict` never raises**: any exception returns a valid uniform distribution. `KEV_DEBUG=1`\n  re-raises so a silent fallback cannot hide a bug during development (it did hide one: a\n  per-member `mix_layers` mismatch that made every prediction uniform).\n* Verified: sibling/order/isolation deviation 2.1e-6 (limit 1e-3), repeat determinism exact,\n  distributions sum to 1 exactly, 564 M registered parameters, 3.5 GB peak inference memory,\n  608 s of the ~1020 s judge inference budget.\n\n## 6. Where the remaining error is\n\nJudge, submission 2: knowledge 1.6051 (mmlu 1.1333 acc 0.498, mmlu_pro 2.0769 acc 0.252),\nother 0.7901. Sources at or below chance: `composition_holdout` 0.50, `fresh_deadline` 0.31,\n`fresh_routing` 0.375, `paws` 0.55. Boolean-rule evaluation and date arithmetic in a single forward\npass of a 0.5B model appear to be out of reach; for those the calibration correctly converges on\nnear-uniform, which is the NLL-optimal response to no skill. The knowledge group is within ~0.04\nnats of the frozen base's own ceiling, so the two remaining levers would be a better backbone\n(fixed) or genuinely learning rule composition (not achieved).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":267,"cache_read_input_tokens":459042,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":267},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"560ecfb8-442b-496c-96fc-76248767870b","uuid":"d2e824d4-7362-428d-ac02-71c25245719d","request_id":"req_011CfHmEFvMSCiAMFVQXNhKb"}

Before calibration five of eleven\ndevelopment sources are *worse than uniform for their arity*.\n\n**F2 — training longer on this corpus destroys transfer.** 1 epoch 0.2766 > 2 epochs ≈ 0.2784 >\n4 epochs with policy oversampling 0.2641, while the training loss falls 1.0 → 0.22. Held-out policy\nfamilies go *below chance* (composition_holdout 0.41, unknowable_control 0.35 accuracy): the model\nlearns family-specific answer patterns and misapplies them to `authorization` / `deadline` /\n`shipping_delay`. Gentler adaptation (lora 16, lr 1e-4, dropout 0.1, 2 epochs) is the best setting.\n\n**F3 — the frozen channel must be fused per question type, outside the training objective.** With a\nsingle shared weight the channel helped every choice source and hurt every yes/no source, because a\npretrained model has a large content-free preference for the first letter. A learned per-type gate\ndid *not* close on its own (it stayed near 1.0 for all three types) because on the *training*\nsources the channel is harmless. Moving the fusion to a post-hoc per-bucket weight fixed it: the\nsearch always selects ~0 for yes/no and ordinal and a large weight for multi-way choice.\n\n**F4 — cyclic-shift symmetrisation is the single biggest win.** Presenting the options under every\ncyclic shift and averaging the per-option log-probabilities back cancels the position prior exactly\nand makes the channel order-invariant. MMLU-Pro 2.235 → 2.154, emotion 1.452 → 1.239,\nQNLI 0.688 → 0.546, SciQ 0.250 → 0.231. Because all shifts go through one batched forward pass it\ncosts under 2 ms per record. Judge reward 0.2913 → 0.3019.\n\n**F5 — single-model differences on this benchmark are seed noise.** Seven members of the same\ngentle recipe span 0.2803-0.2866 on development; the same configuration at a different seed moved\n0.2866 → 0.2807. Per-source means over 64-200 questions give a macro standard error of ~0.015, so\nanything under ~0.02 macro-nll is unmeasurable. This is why the final model is an ensemble rather\nthan the development-best single model: averaging reduces predictor variance, whereas picking the\ndevelopment-best is a noisy selection that does not transfer.\n\n**F6 — question-first encoding is worse.** Re-reading the state conditioned on the instruction\n(one sequence per question, instruction before state) cost 0.008 reward and made `buried` *worse*\n(0.962 vs 0.884). Rejected.\n\n**F7 — date featurisation is not worth it.** The reference ships `kev.api.date_facts`, and the\ncorpus needs date arithmetic (676 compositional atoms are `elapsed` predicates). Wiring it through\ntraining and serving gave 0.2814 vs 0.2812 — no measurable gain, and `legacy_holdout` got worse.\nSince it is also the one transform that could be read as targeting the judge's `date` family, it is\n**deliberately disabled** (`--date_facts 0`); the code path is kept only so the ablation is\nreproducible.\n\n**F8 — fuse only where the channel demonstrably beats uniform.** The search will happily fit a\nweight of 3.6 to binary choice, where the channel's own NLL is 0.690 against a 0.693 uniform floor\nover 96 questions — pure noise. On the judge that weight cost 0.006 nats on `composition_holdout`\nand gained nothing anywhere. The final calibration gates the weight on a ≥2 % relative gain of the\nchannel over uniform within the bucket: noul −1.8 %, binary choice +0.45 %, multi-way choice\n+19.3 %, ordinal −1.3 % → only multi-way choice is fused.\n\n## 5. Robustness decisions (bounded downside rather than best development number)\n\n* **Minimum probability floor 0.01 per bucket.** Costs 0.0001 reward on development and caps a\n  confident error at log(K/0.01) instead of 20.7 nats. Insurance against judge sources the\n  development partition does not contain — and it does contain none of `contrastive`,\n  `fresh_composition`, `fresh_deadline`, `fresh_routing`.\n* **Bootstrap-median calibration.** Twelve scalars fitted on 1156 questions is itself an estimation\n  problem; a split-half check showed the in-sample optimum is optimistic. The shipped scalars are\n  the coordinate median over 24 bootstrap resamples (they came out close to the argmin, which is\n  evidence the optimum is stable).\n* **Encoding truncates, never raises.** The reference entrypoint calls `encode(..., strict=True)`\n  with `MAX_STATE=384 / MAX_BRANCH=1024`; a fresh long record would have raised `ValueError` and\n  invalidated the candidate. Limits are now 1024/1536 and over-long text is truncated.\n* **`predict` never raises**: any exception returns a valid uniform distribution. `KEV_DEBUG=1`\n  re-raises so a silent fallback cannot hide a bug during development (it did hide one: a\n  per-member `mix_layers` mismatch that made every prediction uniform).\n* Verified: sibling/order/isolation deviation 2.1e-6 (limit 1e-3), repeat determinism exact,\n  distributions sum to 1 exactly, 564 M registered parameters, 3.5 GB peak inference memory,\n  608 s of the ~1020 s judge inference budget.\n\n## 6. No text is generated.\n\n## Why it is shaped this way\n\nThe scored workload puts **half** its negative-log-likelihood weight on MMLU and MMLU-Pro, and the\nfixed training corpus contains **no** knowledge multiple-choice data at all. So the knowledge half\ncannot be trained for; it has to be read out of the pretrained base. Meanwhile the transfer half is\ndominated by calibration: before any calibration the reference head is worse than a uniform guess\non five of eleven development sources. Those two facts determine the whole design.\n\n## Components\n\n**1. Trained decision members** (`kev/xmodel.py`, `kev/xtrain.py`) — a LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5-0.5B\nbackbone with a pointer-style readout:\n\n* the record is packed as `<state> … [<q> instructions <opt> option </opt> … <decide>]` per question\n  under a block-causal mask, so sibling questions are exactly independent;\n* option spans are **isolated sub-branches sharing one position range**, so option order cannot\n  change the answer;\n* each option is read from its *whole span* (end token, mean, and a learned attention pool), not\n  from one delimiter token;\n* the head consumes a **learned scalar mix over several backbone layers**, not just the last one;\n* a permutation-equivariant **cross-option transformer block** lets the options be compared before\n  the pointer dot product;\n* the loss is cross-entropy with label smoothing plus a ranked-probability-score term for ordinal\n  questions; soft targets are supported for derived undetermined variants.\n\n**2. A frozen-base letter channel** (`XDecisionModel.letter_logprobs_symmetric`) — the same backbone\nwith **the adapter switched off**, prompted as `state / instructions / A. option … / Answer:` and\nread from the next-token [REDACTED] over \" A\"..\" Z\" via the tied embedding. The option list is\npresented under every cyclic shift and the per-option log-probabilities are averaged back in the\noriginal order, which cancels the model's content-free first-letter preference and makes the channel\norder-invariant. All shifts go through one chunked forward pass, so it costs under 2 ms per record.\nFine-tuning *erodes* this ability (measured: MMLU-Pro 2.148 frozen vs 2.203 adapted), which is why\nthe channel is computed with the adapter disabled rather than from the trained model.\n\n**3. Ensembling** (`kev/xensemble.py`) — five members with different seeds, scalar-mix layer sets,\nhead shapes and augmentation share the one backbone; only adapters and heads are replicated\n(~13 M each), so the whole ensemble fits in 564 M of the 600 M parameter budget. Their\nlog-probability vectors are averaged. Individual members differ only by seed noise on this\nbenchmark, so averaging is preferred to selecting the development-best member.\n\n**4. Calibration and fusion** (`calibrate.py`) — twelve scalars, three per bucket\n(yes/no, binary choice, multi-way choice, ordinal):\n\n```\nz' = (ensemble_logprobs + lm_weight[bucket] * letter_logprobs) / temperature[bucket]\np  = (1 - floor[bucket]) * softmax(z') + floor[bucket] / K\n```\n\nselected on the public development partition (selection only, never trained on) and stored as\nregistered buffers on the served model. Three safeguards: the scalars are the coordinate median over\n24 bootstrap resamples; no bucket may have a zero floor, which bounds the cost of a confident error\non a source the development partition does not contain; and a bucket may only use a non-zero fusion\nweight if the frozen channel beats uniform there by at least 2 % on its own (it does so by 19 % for\nmulti-way choice and not at all for the other three).\n\n## Files\n\n| path | role |\n| --- | --- |\n| `entrypoint.py` | dispatches a checkpoint to the ensemble, single-model, or reference predictor |\n| `train.py` | launcher: verifies the fixed assets, runs two GPU workers, publishes the manifest |\n| `build_ensemble.py` | assembles trained members into one ensemble checkpoint |\n| `calibrate.py` | selects and stores the calibration/fusion scalars |\n| `kev/xmodel.py` | encoding, backbone wrapper, decision head, frozen letter channel |\n| `kev/xtrain.py` | training loop, record-level transforms, distributed accounting |\n| `kev/xensemble.py`, `kev/xserve.py` | serving paths (ensemble / single member) |\n| `kev/serve_ref.py`, `kev/model.py`, `kev/train.py` | the original reference implementation, kept so its control checkpoint still loads |\n\n`python train.py --arch reference` reproduces the reference control run; `python train.py` trains a\nKEV-X member. Research notes and the full experiment log are in `/workspace/experiments/`.\n\n## Constraints honoured\n\nOnly the fixed corpus is read during training (`records_seen == requested_records`, nothing rejected\nor truncated); all retained pretrained weights come from `/opt/kev-assets/base`; the tokenizer and\nvocabulary are unchanged; no external model, teacher, API or answer lookup is involved; encoding\ntruncates rather than raising and `predict` never propagates an exception, so a malformed or\noversized request still returns a valid distribution.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2442,"cache_read_input_tokens":477167,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2442},"output_tokens":17,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"560ecfb8-442b-496c-96fc-76248767870b","uuid":"dc18c6af-8752-4736-917d-e785d4efccb9","request_id":"req_011CfHmWwkgNerdz2kABmUbS"}
